questions.prompt: A 500 N box is pushed up a frictionless ramp 5 m long to a height of 1 m. What effort is needed?
questions.explain: Work in = work out: effort × 5 = 500 × 1, so effort = 100 N.

questions.prompt: A construction worker must raise cement bags to the first floor. Compare using a ramp with using a pulley, and recommend one, using the ideas of effort, distance and efficiency.
questions.modelAnswer: Both reduce the effort. A long ramp gives a large mechanical advantage (small push) but the bags must be pushed a long distance, and friction on the ramp wastes energy. A pulley system with several supporting ropes also reduces the effort, needs less space, and lifts vertically, but the rope must be pulled further than the load rises and pulley friction wastes some energy. On a small site a pulley is often better because it needs little space; the choice depends on space, safety and cost.
rubric: Both reduce effort but increase distance moved
Efficiency is less than 100% because of friction
questions.explain: Criterion D: applying physics to a real decision.
